description: S27 T3 rule 5: a cycle is refused with its closure NAMED, never a bare 'cycle detected'. This edge closes the smallest ring (item 9 already depends on item 12; the attempt is 12 -> 9), so the store's reverse-edge sentence is the closure sentence — the pair, named, with the deadlock it would cause. A longer ring gets the walk's sentence (item X cannot depend on item Y — item Y already depends on item X; the graph would cycle and neither item could ever become ready), proven in internal/roadmap/dependencies_test.go.

data.what: roadmap_dependency: the reverse edge already exists (a 2-cycle would deadlock the graph)
data.means: nothing moved — the row keeps the state it had
